questions.question: How do customers benefit from Amazon's massive economies of scale?

options.text: Periodic price reductions as the result of Amazon's operational efficiencies
New Amazon EC2 instance types providing the latest hardware
The ability to scale up and down when needed
Increased reliability in the underlying hardware of Amazon EC2 instances

questions.explanation: Because AWS aggregates usage from hundreds of thousands of customers, they achieve massive economies of scale. This translates to lower pay-as-you-go prices and periodic price reductions for customers.

questions.question: Which AWS services can be used to gather information about AWS account activity? (Select TWO.)
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs all API activity and user actions within an account, while Amazon CloudWatch collects monitoring and operational data in the form of logs, metrics, and events.

questions.question: Which of the following common IT tasks can AWS cover to free up company IT resources? (Select TWO.)
questions.explanation: When utilizing managed services like Amazon RDS, AWS takes over undifferentiated heavy lifting tasks such as automatically patching the database software and managing routine database backups.

questions.question: In which scenario should Amazon EC2 Spot Instances be used?

options.text: A company wants to move its main website to AWS from an on-premises web server.
A company has a number of application services whose Service Level Agreement (SLA) requires 99.999% uptime.
A company's heavily used legacy database is currently running on-premises.
A company has a number of infrequent, interruptible jobs that are currently using On-Demand Instances.

questions.explanation: Spot Instances allow you to purchase spare compute capacity at steep discounts, but they can be reclaimed by AWS with a 2-minute warning. Therefore, they are only suitable for flexible, interruptible workloads.

questions.question: Which AWS feature should a customer leverage to achieve high availability of an application?
questions.explanation: Deploying applications across multiple Availability Zones ensures high availability. If one AZ experiences an outage, the application can continue running in the remaining AZs.

questions.question: Which is the minimum AWS Support plan that includes Infrastructure Event Management without additional costs?
questions.explanation: AWS Infrastructure Event Management (IEM) offers architecture and scaling guidance for significant operational events. It is included at no additional cost only in the Enterprise Support plan (and available for an extra fee on the Business plan).

questions.question: Which AWS service can serve a static website?
questions.explanation: Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) has a built-in feature that allows you to easily and cost-effectively host static websites (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images) directly from an S3 bucket.

questions.question: How does AWS shorten the time to provision IT resources?

options.text: It supplies an online IT ticketing platform for resource requests.
It supports automatic code validation services.
It provides the ability to programmatically provision existing resources.
It automates the resource request process from a company's IT vendor list.

questions.explanation: AWS allows infrastructure to be treated as code. Using APIs, SDKs, or tools like AWS CloudFormation, teams can programmatically and instantly provision resources rather than waiting for physical hardware installation.

questions.question: What can AWS edge locations be used for? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reducing traffic on the server by caching responses
Sending notification messages to end users

questions.explanation: Edge locations are primarily used by Amazon CloudFront to cache static content geographically closer to end users, which lowers latency and reduces the load on the origin server.

questions.question: Which of the following can limit Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket access to specific users?

options.text: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies

questions.explanation: AWS IAM policies (along with S3 Bucket Policies) are the standard mechanisms used to grant or restrict access to Amazon S3 resources for specific users or roles.

questions.question: A solution that is able to support growth in users, traffic, or data size with no drop in performance aligns with which cloud architecture principle?
questions.explanation: Elasticity allows an architecture to automatically scale its resources horizontally or vertically to handle growth in traffic and user demand without experiencing a degradation in performance.

questions.question: Which of the following tasks is the responsibility of AWS?

options.text: Configuring AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles

questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS is responsible for the security 'of' the cloud, which includes physical infrastructure, the network, and the virtualization layer (the hypervisor).

questions.question: One benefit of On-Demand Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) pricing is:

options.text: the ability to bid for a lower hourly cost.
paying a daily rate regardless of time used.
pre-paying for instances and paying a lower hourly rate.

questions.explanation: On-Demand instances let you pay for compute capacity by the hour or second with no long-term commitments or upfront payments.

questions.question: An administrator needs to rapidly deploy a popular IT solution and start using it immediately. Where can the administrator find assistance?
questions.explanation: AWS Quick Starts are automated reference deployments built by AWS solutions architects that help you deploy popular technologies on AWS rapidly, using best practices.

questions.question: Which of the following services is in the category of AWS serverless platform?
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda is the foundational compute service of the AWS serverless platform, allowing you to run code without provisioning or managing servers.

questions.question: Which services are parts of the AWS serverless platform?

options.text: Amazon EC2, Amazon S3, Amazon Athena
Amazon Kinesis, Amazon SQS, Amazon EMR
AWS Step Functions, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon SNS
Amazon Athena, Amazon Cognito, Amazon EC2

questions.explanation: AWS Step Functions (orchestration), DynamoDB (NoSQL database), and SNS (pub/sub messaging) are all fully managed serverless offerings that scale automatically and require no server management.

questions.question: Under the shared responsibility model, which of the following is a shared control between a customer and AWS?
questions.explanation: Patch management is a shared control. AWS is responsible for patching flaws within the infrastructure, while the customer is responsible for patching their guest OS and applications.

questions.question: What can AWS edge locations be used for? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reducing traffic on the server by caching responses
Sending notification messages to end users

questions.explanation: Edge locations cache duplicate copies of static content closer to users, which improves delivery speeds and dramatically reduces request traffic hitting the origin server.

questions.question: What technology enables compute capacity to adjust as loads change?
questions.explanation: AWS Auto Scaling monitors your applications and automatically adjusts compute capacity to maintain steady, predictable performance at the lowest possible cost.

questions.question: Which AWS services are defined as global instead of regional? (Select TWO.)
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 (DNS) and Amazon CloudFront (CDN) are global services, meaning their interfaces and infrastructure are managed globally rather than being confined to a specific AWS Region.

questions.question: Which AWS service would you use to obtain compliance reports and certificates?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is your go-to, central resource for compliance-related information that matters to you. It provides on-demand access to AWS's security and compliance reports.

questions.question: Under the shared responsibility model, which of the following tasks are the responsibility of the AWS customer? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Ensuring that application data is encrypted at rest
Ensuring that AWS NTP servers are set to the correct time
Ensuring that users have received security training in the use of AWS services
Ensuring that access to data centers is restricted
Ensuring that hardware is disposed of properly

questions.explanation: The customer is responsible for 'Security IN the cloud,' which includes managing their data encryption (at rest and in transit) and ensuring their employees are trained on security best practices.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used to manually launch instances based on resource requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 allows you to manually provision and configure virtual servers (instances) in the cloud based on your specific OS, memory, and CPU needs.

questions.question: A company is migrating an application that is running non-interruptible workloads for a three-year time frame. Which pricing construct would provide the MOST cost-effective solution?
questions.explanation: For steady-state, predictable usage over a 1 or 3-year term, Reserved Instances provide the most significant discount (up to 72%) compared to On-Demand pricing.

questions.question: The financial benefits of using AWS are: (Select TWO.)
questions.explanation: Using AWS reduces the overall Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) by removing the need to manage physical data centers, and it allows businesses to lower their operational expenditures (OpEx) through pay-as-you-go pricing.

questions.question: Which of the following is entirely the responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?

options.text: Patching of the guest operating system
Development of an IAM password policy

questions.explanation: AWS maintains sole responsibility for the physical facilities, including physical access controls, environmental safeguards, and destruction of physical storage media.

questions.question: Which AWS service allows companies to connect an Amazon VPC to an on-premises data center? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated, private network connection to AWS, while AWS VPN creates a secure, encrypted tunnel over the public internet to connect on-premises infrastructure to a VPC.

questions.question: A company wants to reduce the physical compute footprint that developers use to run code. Which service would meet that need by enabling serverless architectures?
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda lets you run code without provisioning or managing any underlying servers, fully removing the need for a physical compute footprint.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides alerts when an AWS event may impact a company's AWS resources?
questions.explanation: The AWS Personal Health Dashboard provides alerts and remediation guidance specifically tailored to events that impact your AWS infrastructure.

questions.question: Which of the following are categories of AWS Trusted Advisor? (Select TWO.)
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor analyzes your account and provides checks across 5 categories: Cost Optimization, Performance, Security, Fault Tolerance, and Service Limits.

questions.question: Which of the following services falls under the responsibility of the customer to maintain operating system configuration, security patching, and networking?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 is an Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) offering. Because it provides unmanaged compute capacity, the customer is fully responsible for configuring and patching the guest operating system.

questions.question: A company will be moving from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. What would be one financial difference after the move?

options.text: Moving from variable operational expense (opex) to upfront capital expense (capex).
Moving from upfront capital expense (capex) to variable capital expense (capex).
Moving from upfront capital expense (capex) to variable operational expense (opex).
Elimination of upfront capital expense (capex) and elimination of variable operational expense (opex)

questions.explanation: The cloud financial model shifts costs away from large, upfront Capital Expenditures (building data centers) into flexible, variable Operational Expenditures (paying only for the compute you consume).

questions.question: How should a customer forecast the future costs for running a new web application?
questions.explanation: The AWS Simple Monthly Calculator (now integrated into the AWS Pricing Calculator) allows users to build an estimate of what their architecture will cost before actually deploying resources.

questions.question: Which is the MINIMUM AWS Support plan that provides technical support through phone calls?
questions.explanation: The Business Support plan is the lowest tier that unlocks 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers via phone, chat, and email.

questions.question: According to the AWS shared responsibility model, what is the sole responsibility of AWS?
questions.explanation: AWS takes sole responsibility for the security, provisioning, and management of the physical components of the AWS Global Infrastructure, which includes Regions, Availability Zones, and Edge Locations.

questions.question: Which AWS IAM feature is used to associate a set of permissions with multiple users?
questions.explanation: IAM Groups are collections of IAM users. By attaching an IAM policy to a group, you instantly apply those permissions to every user within that group.

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits of the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Elasticity (the ability to scale up and down easily) and Agility (speed to provision resources and innovate) are two core benefits of migrating to the AWS cloud.

questions.question: Which of the following can a customer use to enable single sign-on (SSO) to the AWS Console?
questions.explanation: AWS Directory Service (specifically AWS Managed Microsoft AD) can be used to set up federation and Single Sign-On, allowing existing corporate credentials to access the AWS Management Console.

questions.question: What are the multiple, isolated locations within an AWS Region that are connected by low-latency networks called?
questions.explanation: An AWS Region is a physical location in the world that consists of multiple, isolated, and physically separate data center clusters known as Availability Zones.

questions.question: Which of the following benefits does the AWS Compliance program provide to AWS customers? (Choose two.)

options.text: It verifies that hosted workloads are automatically compliant with the controls of supported compliance frameworks.
AWS is responsible for the maintenance of common compliance framework documentation.
It assures customers that AWS is maintaining physical security and data protection.
It ensures the use of compliance frameworks that are being used by other cloud providers.
It will adopt new compliance frameworks as they become relevant to customer workloads.

questions.explanation: The AWS Compliance program assures customers that AWS physically secures the underlying infrastructure (C), and it is continually adapting to include new compliance frameworks as global regulations evolve (E). Note: Workloads are *never* automatically compliant; the customer must configure them correctly.

questions.question: Which of the following services provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is your centralized resource for compliance-related information, offering on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance reports.

questions.question: As part of the AWS shared responsibility model, which of the following operational controls do users fully inherit from AWS?
questions.explanation: Users fully inherit physical and environmental controls from AWS, meaning AWS completely handles the physical security of the data centers.

questions.question: When comparing AWS Cloud with on-premises Total Cost of Ownership, which expenses must be considered? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: An on-premises TCO calculation must account for the heavy capital expenditures of purchasing and maintaining physical storage hardware and physical servers.

questions.question: Under the shared responsibility model, which of the following tasks are the responsibility of the customer? (Choose two.)

options.text: Maintaining the underlying Amazon EC2 hardware.
Managing the VPC network access control lists.
Encrypting data in transit and at rest.
Deploying hardware in different Availability Zones.

questions.explanation: Customers are responsible for 'Security IN the cloud,' which includes managing software-defined network firewalls (like ACLs and Security Groups) and securing their data via encryption.

questions.question: Which scenarios represent the concept of elasticity on AWS? (Choose two.)

options.text: Scaling the number of Amazon EC2 instances based on traffic.
Resizing Amazon RDS instances as business needs change.
Automatically directing traffic to less-utilized Amazon EC2 instances.
Using AWS compliance documents to accelerate the compliance process.
Having the ability to create and govern environments using code.

questions.explanation: Elasticity involves dynamically scaling resources up/down (like resizing RDS) or out/in (like adding EC2 instances) to match the immediate capacity needs of the workload.

questions.question: When is it beneficial for a company to use a Spot Instance?

options.text: When there is flexibility in when an application needs to run.
When an instance should not be stopped.

questions.explanation: Because Spot Instances can be interrupted by AWS at any time, they are only beneficial when a workload is flexible, interruptible, or stateless (like batch processing jobs).

questions.question: A company is considering moving its on-premises data center to AWS. What factors should be included in doing a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis? (Choose two.)

options.text: Power consumption of the data center
Labor costs to replace old servers

questions.explanation: A TCO analysis must factor in all operational expenses that are eliminated by moving to the cloud, such as the electricity required to cool and power a data center, and the physical labor required to rack and stack servers.

questions.question: How does AWS charge for AWS Lambda?

options.text: Users bid on the maximum price they are willing to pay per hour.
Users choose a 1-, 3- or 5-year upfront payment term.
Users pay for the required permanent storage on a file system or in a database.
Users pay based on the number of requests and consumed compute resources.

questions.explanation: AWS Lambda pricing is entirely execution-based. You are charged based on the total number of requests (invocations) and the duration (compute time measured in milliseconds) that your code executes.

questions.question: What function do security groups serve related Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance security?

options.text: Act as a virtual firewall for the Amazon EC2 instance.
Secure AWS user accounts with AWS identity and Access Management (IAM) policies.
Provide DDoS protection with AWS Shield.
Use Amazon CloudFront to protect the Amazon EC2 instance.

questions.explanation: A security group acts as a stateful, virtual firewall at the instance level to control inbound and outbound traffic for one or more EC2 instances.

questions.question: Which disaster recovery scenario offers the lowest probability of down time?
questions.explanation: Multi-site active-active involves running full workloads simultaneously across two or more sites. It provides the lowest probability of downtime (near-zero RTO and RPO) because traffic is already being actively served from multiple locations.
